paragraphs: An AI system can combine several models and tools, yet people ultimately judge the result produced by the whole arrangement. Aligning each component separately does not directly solve this problem: a preference between complete outputs does not automatically identify preferred behavior for every component. Some interactions also prevent gradients from flowing through the entire system.

The paper introduces SysDPO, which extends Direct Preference Optimization to joint alignment of compound systems. It first represents the system as a directed acyclic graph, making the components, their interactions, and the movement of data explicit. This representation provides the basis for optimizing against preferences expressed at the system level. Two variants, SysDPO-Direct and SysDPO-Sampling, address settings that differ in whether a system-specific preference dataset is constructed.

The authors demonstrate the approach in two applications: aligning a language model together with a diffusion model, and aligning a collaboration among language models. These experiments support treating alignment as a property of interacting components, with training directed toward the quality of their combined output.
neurips-2025-aligning-compound-ai-system.tldr: SysDPO extends preference optimization to jointly align interacting AI components using preferences over whole-system outputs.

paragraphs: Photographic settings vary continuously, but text-driven image editors typically receive instructions through discrete tokens. This makes it difficult to request smooth, fine adjustments to camera-related effects. CamEdit addresses that mismatch by giving a diffusion-based image editor continuous controls with meanings tied to camera parameters.

The framework combines continuous parameter prompting with a parameter-aware modulation module. Together, they guide changes to focal plane, aperture, and shutter speed within the diffusion process. The aim is to make incremental changes in these settings produce consistent changes in the edited image, supporting photographic control beyond a collection of separate verbal descriptions.

The authors also introduce CamEdit50K to provide supervised examples for this task. It contains more than 50,000 image pairs drawn from real and synthetic data, with densely varied camera settings across diverse scenes. Experiments report flexible, consistent, high-fidelity editing and state-of-the-art performance in camera-aware manipulation. The contribution therefore includes both a control mechanism and training data designed around continuous photographic adjustments.
neurips-2025-camedit-continuous-camera-p.tldr: CamEdit gives diffusion-based image editing continuous camera controls, supported by a dataset of densely varied photographic settings.

paragraphs: An action-recognition model may rely on how a person moves, the objects nearby, or the surrounding scene. Explanations that mix these sources make it difficult to understand the prediction. Describing everything in words introduces another problem: movement can be recognizable without being easy to verbalize precisely.

DANCE separates the evidence into motion dynamics, objects, and scenes. It represents motion concepts as sequences of human poses, while a large language model automatically extracts object and scene concepts. These concepts form a bottleneck through which the model must make its prediction. Consequently, the explanation structure is built into the recognition process, rather than added only after an action has been predicted.

Experiments on KTH, Penn Action, HAA500, and UCF101 report clearer explanations while maintaining competitive recognition performance. A user study also supports improved interpretability. The authors further demonstrate benefits for debugging, editing, and analyzing failures, where distinguishing movement evidence from contextual evidence helps explain why the model reached a particular decision.
neurips-2025-disentangled-concepts-speak.tldr: DANCE makes video action predictions through separate motion, object, and scene concepts to improve explanation clarity.

paragraphs: Tensor decomposition represents multidimensional data using a smaller collection of interacting factors. Temporal versions can describe how those factors change over time, but continuous coordinates may also appear in other dimensions, such as location. Catte addresses both this broader coordinate structure and the question of how much model complexity the data requires.

The method encodes continuous spatial coordinates using learnable Fourier features and models the factors' time evolution with neural ordinary differential equations. A sparsity-inducing prior over these trajectories encourages a compact representation, allowing complexity to adapt during learning. Its variational inference procedure uses an analytical evidence lower bound, so optimizing that objective does not require sampling.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets report that Catte identifies underlying tensor ranks and substantially improves prediction and resistance to noise over existing methods. These findings connect its two design goals: accommodating continuously indexed data and learning an appropriate number of effective factors, rather than treating representational complexity as a separate fixed choice.
neurips-2025-functional-complexity-adapt.tldr: Catte models continuously indexed temporal tensors while adapting factor complexity through a sparsity-inducing prior.

paragraphs: Low-Rank Adaptation fine-tunes a language model through compact adapter weights. Its effectiveness depends on both the rank assigned to those adapters and how their weights are initialized. The paper argues that treating these decisions separately can leave shortcomings in performance, usability, or computational efficiency.

GoRA combines rank adaptation and initialization in one framework. It uses gradient information during training to guide the allocation of ranks and the adaptive initialization of adapter weights. This connects the amount of adaptation capacity with the starting values used for that capacity, making both decisions responsive to training information.

Across the architectures and modalities evaluated, the authors report consistent improvements over existing LoRA-based methods while preserving standard LoRA's efficiency. For mathematical reasoning with Llama3.1-8B-Base, GoRA improves on standard LoRA by 5.13 points. Under high-rank settings, it also exceeds full fine-tuning by 2.05 points. These results support coordinating rank and initialization as a practical way to improve efficient adaptation in the tested settings.
neurips-2025-gora-gradient-driven-adapti.tldr: GoRA uses training gradients to jointly adapt LoRA ranks and adapter initialization, improving fine-tuning results while retaining efficiency.

paragraphs: Training-free guidance lets users steer a diffusion or flow model without retraining it. For gradient-based guidance, two common approaches appear quite different. Posterior guidance uses a target prediction model to guide the current sample toward the desired distribution. End-to-end guidance backpropagates through the entire ordinary differential equation solve.

The paper connects these approaches by showing how posterior guidance can be understood as a greedy strategy for end-to-end guidance. This supplies a shared perspective for analyzing their relationship to ideal continuous gradients. The distinction between the methods becomes a question about how guidance gradients are approximated across the generation process.

Building on that analysis, the authors introduce a method that interpolates between the two families. It offers a trade-off between computational effort and guidance-gradient accuracy, rather than requiring a choice between only the endpoints. Validation on inverse image problems and property-guided molecular generation demonstrates the relevance of this connection across both visual reconstruction and the steering of molecular properties.
neurips-2025-greed-is-good-a-unifying-pe.tldr: The paper unifies posterior and end-to-end generation guidance and introduces a way to trade gradient accuracy against computation.

paragraphs: Deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting describes a moving scene through a static reference representation and motion that changes over time. Compact motion representations are useful, but learning all motion information through gradients creates many degrees of freedom. Existing approaches can consequently struggle to converge on real scenes with complex movement.

H3D-DGS introduces control points whose motion attributes are obtained through two complementary routes. Motion components that project onto the image plane come directly from back-projecting optical flow. Components that are unobservable are refined through gradient-based optimization. This separates motion supported by direct image evidence from motion that still needs to be optimized, while keeping the representation compact.

Experiments on Neu3DV and CMU-Panoptic report superior performance over state-of-the-art deformable Gaussian splatting methods. The authors also report convergence within 100 iterations and processing of each frame in two seconds on one NVIDIA RTX 4070 GPU. These findings support combining observed motion and learned motion as a way to address convergence difficulties in the evaluated reconstruction tasks.
neurips-2025-h3d-dgs-exploring-heterogen.tldr: H3D-DGS combines optical-flow-derived motion with gradient-based refinement to improve dynamic Gaussian scene reconstruction and convergence.

paragraphs: Designing a group of collaborating language models involves deciding both how they interact and how their model weights should be adapted. Heterogeneous Swarms searches over these decisions together. It represents a system as a directed acyclic graph, where connections determine how inputs and generated outputs move between models.

The algorithm alternates between a role step and a weight step. During the role step, candidate continuous connection matrices are converted into discrete graphs, executed in dependency order, and evaluated using a chosen utility function. Particle swarm optimization updates the candidates from those scores. During the weight step, a proposed JFK-score measures each model's contribution in the best graph found, providing the signal for optimizing model weights through swarm intelligence.

Across 12 tasks, the authors report an average 18.5% advantage over 17 baselines that optimize roles, weights, or both. Further analysis finds varied model roles and substantial benefits from collaboration. The results also indicate that diversity among the available language models helps the search discover effective systems.
neurips-2025-heterogeneous-swarms-jointl.tldr: Heterogeneous Swarms jointly searches collaboration graphs and model weights to build more effective multi-LLM systems.

paragraphs: Cooperating agents sometimes need similar behavior and sometimes need specialized roles. Sharing policy parameters makes learning efficient, but updates from different agents can interfere and suppress this diversity. The authors find that the common practice of combining agent identifiers with observations can make that gradient interference worse.

HyperMARL uses an agent-conditioned hypernetwork to generate parameters specific to each agent. This separates gradients associated with agent identity from those associated with observations, directly addressing the coupling identified in the paper. The approach avoids relying on manually preset diversity levels, changed objectives, or sequential updates, and empirically reduces policy-gradient variance.

The evaluation covers 22 scenarios with as many as 30 agents. HyperMARL achieves performance competitive with six key baselines while retaining behavioral diversity comparable to methods that do not share parameters. These findings suggest that a shared parameter-generating mechanism can support differentiated agent policies, allowing efficient learning and specialization to coexist in the tested cooperative settings.
neurips-2025-hypermarl-adaptive-hypernet.tldr: HyperMARL generates agent-specific policy parameters with a shared hypernetwork to reduce gradient interference and preserve behavioral diversity.

paragraphs: Natural gradient methods can speed up training of physics-informed neural networks, but computing their updates can itself become prohibitively expensive. This paper improves energy natural gradient descent, or ENGD, by targeting both the cost of each update and the speed at which training converges.

The first technique uses the Woodbury formula to substantially reduce computational complexity. The second adapts Subsampled Projected-Increment Natural Gradient Descent from variational Monte Carlo to accelerate convergence. The authors also investigate randomized algorithms for reducing computational cost when batches are large. These are complementary changes to the optimization procedure, each addressing a different source of training expense.

Numerical experiments report reaching the same L2 error as original ENGD up to 75 times faster. The findings about randomization are more specific: it accelerates early training on low-dimensional problems, while other scenarios present barriers to obtaining acceleration. Thus, the paper offers substantial overall speed improvements alongside a qualified account of when randomization contributes useful gains.
neurips-2025-improving-energy-natural-gr.tldr: The paper accelerates energy natural gradient training for physics-informed networks, reporting up to 75-fold faster attainment of the same error.

paragraphs: Language models still struggle with complex reasoning that requires several connected logical steps. Synthetic training data offers one route to improvement, but predefined templates can restrict how well examples reflect varied real-world situations. LogicTree aims to generate both richer reasoning structures and meaningful contextual versions of those structures.

The framework builds logic trees through backward deduction. At each stage, structural pattern matching identifies applicable logical rules, allowing the process to expand into a multistep reasoning pattern. A two-stage language-model procedure then turns each tree into different real-world scenarios while maintaining consistent reasoning. This separates the construction of a logical structure from the task of expressing it in a concrete context.

Experiments across multiple benchmarks report an average 9.4% accuracy improvement on complex logical reasoning tasks. The stated purpose of contextualizing the trees is to help models learn reasoning that transfers across scenarios, rather than merely memorize templates. The findings support this structured synthetic-data approach as a way to strengthen multistep reasoning.
neurips-2025-logictree-improving-complex.tldr: LogicTree builds multistep logical structures and instantiates them in varied scenarios to create training data for stronger reasoning.

paragraphs: Multi-agent inverse reinforcement learning asks what rewards could explain the behavior of interacting experts. The difficulty is that observing an equilibrium does not uniquely reveal those rewards. Several different reward structures can justify the same behavior, and those structures may imply different kinds of strategic interaction.

The paper characterizes the feasible reward set in Markov games: all reward functions that make a given equilibrium rational. This turns ambiguity into an explicit mathematical object to study. It then introduces entropy-regularized Markov games, which, in the setting developed by the authors, produce a unique equilibrium while preserving strategic incentives.

For this regularized setting, the authors analyze sample complexity and how estimation errors influence the performance of learned policies. The contribution connects three questions: which rewards fit observed behavior, how equilibrium ambiguity can be addressed, and how imperfect learning affects subsequent decisions. Its uniqueness claim concerns equilibrium in the proposed setting; the starting observation remains that a single observed equilibrium can be compatible with many reward structures.
neurips-2025-on-feasible-rewards-in-mult.tldr: The paper characterizes rewards compatible with multi-agent equilibria and analyzes learning in an entropy-regularized setting with a unique equilibrium.

paragraphs: Reducing image tokens can make vision models more efficient, but Mamba-based models can lose substantially more accuracy than Vision Transformers. The authors hypothesize that Mamba's chain-like scanning creates cascading connectivity losses when tokens disappear and restricts the variety of spatial regions represented by its features.

AMVim addresses this with two different scanning paths. One uses a window-aware mechanism, while the other retains sequential scanning. The asymmetric arrangement increases the diversity of token connections and allows information to move at multiple spatial scales. Its design therefore targets how remaining tokens communicate when some tokens have been removed.

Experiments report state-of-the-art pruning robustness. During token reduction, AMVim-T achieves a 34% improvement in training-free accuracy at identical model sizes and FLOPs, while AMVim-S loses only 1.5% accuracy and performs comparably to a Vision Transformer. The architecture also improves performance without pruning. These empirical results support the design, while the proposed explanation for the original connectivity problem remains a hypothesis.
neurips-2025-pruning-robust-mamba-with-a.tldr: AMVim combines window-aware and sequential scanning to make vision Mamba models more robust to token removal.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning for language-model reasoning must decide which parts of a response deserve credit. Token-level methods seek detailed feedback but depend on a critic that can be difficult to train accurately. Whole-response methods use final rewards, leaving less information about which intermediate steps contributed to success.

Segment Policy Optimization assigns advantages to segments between these two extremes. Fewer estimation points make Monte Carlo estimation possible without a critic, while retaining more precise credit assignment than a single trajectory-level signal. The framework combines flexible segmentation, segment-advantage estimation, and policy updates that include a probability-mask strategy.

The paper develops separate versions for short and long reasoning. SPO-chain uses cutpoints and chain-based estimation, improving GSM8K accuracy by 6–12 percentage points over PPO and GRPO. SPO-tree uses tree-based estimation to substantially reduce Monte Carlo cost, improving MATH500 accuracy by 7–11 percentage points over GRPO under 2K and 4K context evaluation. These results support segment granularity as a useful balance between feedback precision and estimation effort.
neurips-2025-segment-policy-optimization.tldr: SPO trains reasoning models using segment-level credit assignment, enabling critic-free estimation and reported accuracy gains on reasoning benchmarks.

paragraphs: Training a tool-using language-model agent usually requires people to create varied tasks and decide how success should be evaluated. The Self-Challenging Agent framework shifts task creation into the training process itself. An agent generates challenges and then learns to solve the tasks that pass quality checks.

In its challenger role, the agent interacts with the available tools before proposing a task. Each task uses the Code-as-Task format: an instruction, a verification function, and examples of successful and unsuccessful solutions that serve as tests. This structure makes task quality something the framework can check. The agent then switches to an executor role and uses reinforcement learning, with evaluation feedback supplying the reward.

Using only self-generated training data, the method improves Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on M³ToolEval and TauBench, two benchmarks involving multiple turns of tool use. The reported average success rate doubles. This demonstrates that the framework's generated, testable challenges can provide useful training signals for improving tool-use behavior on the evaluated benchmarks.
neurips-2025-self-challenging-language-m.tldr: A self-challenging agent creates verifiable tool-use tasks and learns from them, doubling average success on two evaluated benchmarks.

paragraphs: Some learning problems involve a finite collection of decision variables but infinitely many constraints. Semi-infinite programming provides a way to express such requirements. This paper studies a nonconvex min-max setting with nonconvex infinite constraints, motivated by adversarial robustness and learning subject to safety constraints.

The authors propose an inexact dynamic barrier primal-dual algorithm and prove convergence properties under a specific assumption: the squared infeasibility residual satisfies the Lojasiewicz inequality with exponent θ between zero and one. The guarantees address approximate stationarity, constraint infeasibility, and complementarity slackness, which respectively concern optimization progress, constraint violation, and the relationship between constraints and their multipliers.

For accuracy tolerance ε, the stated iteration bounds are O(ε^-3), O(ε^(-6θ)), and O(ε^(-3θ/(1−θ))) for those three criteria. These are conditional guarantees for approximate conditions, rather than a claim of finding a global optimum. Numerical experiments on robust multitask learning with task priorities also illustrate practical effectiveness, connecting the analysis to a learning problem with competing objectives and constraints.
neurips-2025-semi-infinite-nonconvex-con.tldr: The paper proposes a primal-dual algorithm for nonconvex min-max problems with infinitely many constraints and proves conditional iteration bounds.

paragraphs: Stable Part Diffusion 4D generates paired color videos and part maps from monocular inputs. Its parts follow an object's articulation and remain consistent across viewpoints and time. This emphasizes components relevant to movement, rather than grouping regions only through appearance-based semantic cues.

A dual-branch diffusion model generates RGB frames and their part segmentations together. Spatial color encoding expresses part masks as continuous RGB-like images, allowing both branches to share a latent variational autoencoder and supporting different numbers of parts. A bidirectional fusion module links the branches, while a contrastive consistency loss encourages part predictions to align across space and time.

The authors build KinematicParts20K from more than 20,000 rigged Objaverse XL objects, paired with multiview color and part videos. Experiments show generalization to real videos, newly generated objects, and rare articulated poses. Generated 2D maps can also be lifted into 3D to derive skeletons and harmonic skinning weights with few manual adjustments, connecting the outputs to animation and motion-related uses.
neurips-2025-stable-part-diffusion-4d-mu.tldr: SP4D jointly generates multiview color videos and articulation-aware part maps that can support downstream 3D animation.

paragraphs: Distributing long-sequence Transformer training across hardware creates a communication problem as well as a computation problem. Existing approaches can be limited by the number of attention heads or by excessive data exchange. StarTrail changes how distributed workers communicate to improve efficiency and scalability for long inputs.

The system introduces an additional parallel dimension and organizes peer-to-peer exchanges into smaller sub-rings. This concentric arrangement reduces communication volume and helps avoid bandwidth bottlenecks. It also gives more flexibility in tuning communication arrangements, so the distributed organization can be adjusted across hardware environments.

Experiments span natural language processing and computer vision tasks on diverse hardware. The authors report performance improvements of up to 77.12% for GPT-style models and 114.33% for Diffusion Transformer models over state-of-the-art methods supporting long sequences, without changing computation results. These are gains in distributed training performance: the contribution is a more efficient way to execute the model's computations, making communication organization central to scaling long-sequence training.
neurips-2025-startrail-concentric-ring-s.tldr: StarTrail reorganizes distributed communication into concentric sub-rings to accelerate long-sequence Transformer training without changing computation results.

paragraphs: This position paper argues that clinical AI needs a stronger statistical foundation for monitoring after deployment. It cites a review in which only 9% of FDA-registered AI-based healthcare tools included a surveillance plan. Manual, occasional, reactive checks are presented as poorly suited to the changing environments where clinical models operate.

The proposed foundation is label-efficient statistical testing with explicit error-rate guarantees, inference under predefined assumptions, and reproducible procedures. The authors distinguish detecting changes in incoming data from detecting deterioration in model performance. Framing these as separate hypothesis-testing problems makes clear that they ask different questions and should have their own statistical treatment.

The paper's contribution is a methodological position and research agenda. It calls for monitoring methods that provide a reproducible basis for assessing reliability while limiting labeling demands. It also identifies opportunities to develop theory and tools for detecting failures, attributing their causes, and mitigating their effects. The proposed guarantees depend on stated assumptions, making those assumptions part of the monitoring framework.
neurips-2025-statistically-valid-post-de.tldr: The paper argues for label-efficient, statistically valid monitoring that separately tests for data changes and clinical AI performance degradation.

paragraphs: Preference optimization for vision-language models depends on the reward differences between preferred and rejected responses. Merely ranking or rewriting answers does not necessarily provide precise control over those differences. This paper focuses on deliberately shaping the reward gaps throughout a preference dataset to improve hallucination reduction.

Topic-level Preference Rewriting, or TPR, selectively replaces semantic topics within responses using candidates resampled from the model itself. Working at this level gives finer control over response content than treating each answer as an indivisible unit. It supports strategies such as progressively changing the difficulty of rejected responses, thereby adjusting the comparisons from which the model learns.

Across multiple hallucination benchmarks, the authors report state-of-the-art results and an average improvement of approximately 20% over previous methods. On ObjectHal-Bench, hallucinations decrease by up to 93%. They also report better data efficiency. These findings support carefully designing preference pairs as an important part of alignment, with topic-level editing providing a practical mechanism for controlling their training signal.
neurips-2025-systematic-reward-gap-optim.tldr: TPR rewrites selected response topics to control preference reward gaps and improve hallucination reduction in vision-language models.

paragraphs: Selecting instruction-tuning examples can reduce redundant training data, but a high score for an entire example can hide two problems. Some tokens contribute little useful information, and superficial wording can distort the score. T-SHIRT addresses both the informativeness of individual tokens and the reliability of sample-level quality judgments.

Its scoring method considers only informative tokens when evaluating quality. It also favors examples whose neighboring samples receive consistently high scores, reducing reliance on isolated high scores with local inconsistencies. This hierarchical selection process combines evidence within an example with evidence about the stability of its quality assessment.

Models trained on T-SHIRT selections containing only 5% of the original data outperform full-dataset training by up to 5.48 points on average across eight benchmarks. The authors also report consistent advantages over existing selection methods across models and training scales. For scoring efficiency, a GPT-2-based setup processes 52,000 examples in 40 minutes on one GPU. Together, these results support selective curation as a means to improve both training efficiency and evaluated performance.
neurips-2025-t-shirt-token-selective-hie.tldr: T-SHIRT selects instruction data using informative tokens and locally consistent quality scores, achieving strong results with only 5% of the data.

paragraphs: Tensor parallelism distributes language-model computations but requires substantial communication to synchronize intermediate activations. That synchronization creates bandwidth demands during both training and inference. This paper investigates whether the model architecture can be adjusted so that activations do not always need to be fully synchronized.

The proposed Communication-Aware Architecture for Tensor-parallelism, or CAAT-Net, uses a few modifications to current practice to permit partial synchronization. The central idea is to make reduced communication part of the architecture used for learning. This changes the relationship between model computation and distributed execution, allowing the training process to work with less activation exchange.

For a seven-billion-parameter model, communication falls by up to 50% without a significant decrease in pretraining accuracy across nearly all evaluated benchmarks. Experiments with 130-million- and 1.1-billion-parameter models also support the approach across scales. Validation loss even improves in some scenarios, and training and inference accelerate across various settings. The findings support partial synchronization as a useful bandwidth-saving design choice in the evaluated configurations.
neurips-2025-tensor-parallelism-with-par.tldr: CAAT-Net enables partial activation synchronization, reducing tensor-parallel communication by up to 50% with little evaluated accuracy impact.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to estimate a quantile while protecting individual data through local differential privacy and tracking uncertainty as observations arrive. Its target is a confidence sequence: a succession of uncertainty intervals designed for monitoring over time. The stated validity is asymptotic, an important qualification to its anytime interpretation.

The algorithm combines dynamically chained parallel stochastic gradient descent with randomized response. The privacy mechanism protects the data, while the online procedure jointly estimates the target quantile and the variance of its estimator. Estimating both quantities allows the method to produce an uncertainty assessment alongside its changing quantile estimate.

A strong Gaussian approximation supports the asymptotically anytime-valid confidence sequences, whose widths follow law-of-the-iterated-logarithm behavior. The method requires only O(κ) memory, where κ is the number of chains and is much smaller than the sample size. Mathematical proofs and numerical experiments support the procedure, connecting privacy protection, ongoing statistical inference, and efficient processing in a single online algorithm.
neurips-2025-time-uniform-and-asymptotic.tldr: The paper develops a memory-efficient online quantile estimator with local privacy and asymptotically anytime-valid confidence sequences.

paragraphs: Language-model reinforcement learning can generate experience in parallel with training, but that experience may come from policies that differ from the current learner. Standard on-policy methods are not naturally robust to the resulting diversity in replay buffers. This makes efficient asynchronous data generation difficult to exploit fully.

Trajectory Balance with Asynchrony, or TBA, uses an off-policy trajectory-balance objective to learn from such data. It decouples exploration from learning so that actors can keep supplying experience while training proceeds. Sampling that prioritizes reward and recency provides another way to select useful experience as the amount of generated data grows.

The authors evaluate math, preference-tuning, and automated red-teaming tasks with models ranging from Pythia 410M to Qwen 2.5 7B. They report speed and performance gains over Online DPO and Dr. GRPO, including speedups of four times or more and high accuracy as asynchrony increases. Reward- and recency-based sampling brings further gains when data generation scales, supporting the value of coordinating off-policy learning with asynchronous experience collection.
neurips-2025-trajectory-balance-with-asy.tldr: TBA uses off-policy trajectory balance to learn efficiently from asynchronously generated experience, reporting speedups of four times or more.

paragraphs: Dense visual correspondence requires features that distinguish locations across images. The authors find that diffusion Transformers can produce a few extremely large feature activations that undermine this task. These activations repeatedly occupy a small set of fixed dimensions across image patches and carry little local information.

The paper links this concentration to adaptive layer normalization, or AdaLN. Its training-free DiTF framework uses AdaLN-based channel modulation to locate and normalize the oversized activations. A further channel-discard strategy reduces their adverse effects. Together, these changes aim to expose semantically useful features already present in the pretrained model.

Experiments report that DiTF outperforms DINO and Stable Diffusion-based models and establishes state-of-the-art results for diffusion Transformers on different correspondence tasks. Reported improvements include 9.4% on Spair-71k and 4.4% on AP-10K-C.S. The findings identify activation imbalance as a concrete obstacle to extracting useful correspondence features and show that addressing it can improve performance without training the proposed feature-extraction framework.
neurips-2025-unleashing-diffusion-transf.tldr: DiTF improves diffusion Transformer features for visual matching by normalizing and discarding channels affected by unusually large activations.
